newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Malaysia says considers oil cooperation with Kuwait.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says considers oil cooperation with Kuwait.

text.p: Malaysia and Kuwait are considering joint upstream and downstream oil cooperation in third countries, Malaysia's prime minister said on Monday.
"We see the possibility of the two national petroleum companies cooperating with each other in third countries either upstream or downstream," Mahathir Mohamad told a news conference in Kuwait.
"We think that with our cooperation we will lend strength to our ventures and to third countries in particular so that we can exploit the potentials of oil and gas in other countries."
But Mohamad said at the end of his official visit that "we have not signed anything" during the trip.
"We may want to buy more petroleum from Kuwait," he said without specifying the amount that Kuala Lumpur sought.
A Malaysian embassy official said Malaysia imported $22.59 million worth of oil products and $1.15 million worth of crude oil from Kuwait in the eight months to August 1996.
Oil imports account for 80 percent of total Malaysian imports from the oil-rich Gulf Arab state, said Mohamad.
